channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Canada CPI expected to show rising inflation in July
item.description: Canada’s July Consumer Price Index (CPI) figures will be the focus of attention when published on Monday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks cap losses against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that September Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike odds have risen sharply, but the Japanese Yen (JPY) has reacted only modestly. They argue a sustained Yen recovery likely needs clearer commitment to faster policy normalisation.

item.title: Indian Rupee steadies as RBI swap exit, soft US data cap USD/INR
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) remains stronger against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday after two days of losses, with the USD/INR pair trading around 95.60 at the time of writing.

item.title: 0.8550: Euro tests one-week highs against British Pound amid ECB hawkish bets
item.description: The Euro (EUR) holds minor gains against the British Pound (GBP) for the third consecutive day on Monday, favoured by European Central Bank (ECB) - Bank of England (BoE) monetary policy divergence.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar extends pullback to start new week
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Monday, August 17:

item.title: Gold looks to build strength above $4,400 as fading Fed hike bets keeps USD depressed
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) builds on Friday's bounce from the $4,300 neighborhood and attracts some follow-through buyers at the start of a new week.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Data and tariffs shape near-term risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Robert Both and Emma Lawrence highlight that markets are watching Canadian CPI and potential US Section 338 tariffs on CAD exports. They expect headline CPI at 2.9% year-on-year in July with core at 1.85%, and see retail sales flat in June.

item.title: 0.6%: China’s Retail Sales miss expectations in July
item.description: China’s Retail Sales rose 0.6% year-over-year (YoY) in July vs. A rise of 1.5% expected and a 1.0% growth in June, the latest data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed Monday.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank steady as currency lags – BNY
item.description: BNY's Wee Khoon Chong note Sweden’s Riksbank appears comfortable with its current policy stance as inflation stays below target, leaving two hikes in the repo path mainly as a risk acknowledgment.

item.title: Canadian Dollar edges higher as Fed rate hike bets recede, CPI data looms
item.description: The USD/CAD pair edges lower to around 1.3860 during the early European session on Monday. The US Dollar (USD) extends the decline against the Canadian Dollar (CAD) as traders pare bets on the US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes.

item.title: Equities: Mixed performance across regions – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight a mixed global equity picture, with the Nikkei, CSI 300, Shanghai Composite and Hang Seng all advancing, while US equity futures, led by NASDAQ, also point higher.

item.title: British Pound: Data mix limits sustained gains against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad says improving United Kingdom (UK) disinflation alongside solid Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) should support the British Pound (GBP) against the US Dollar (USD) and Euro (EUR), but sees limited scope for a lasting rally.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Nominal growth underpins cautious strength – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur says solid nominal growth and higher-than-expected inflation should keep pressure on the Bank of Japan (BoJ) to raise rates again as early as September or October.

item.title: Silver Price Forecasts: XAG/USD approaches $66.00 favoured by a softer US Dollar
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades on a strong footing on Monday, reaching levels above $65.80 at the European session opening times, after bouncing from the $63.50 area on Friday.

item.title: Euro: Upside bias targets 1.1590 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang highlights that EUR/USD surged to 1.1585, leaving the Euro (EUR) with a firmer tone against the US Dollar (USD). Intraday, the pair could extend gains toward 1.1590, though 1.1610 is seen as strong resistance.

item.title: British Pound gathers strength above 1.3550 as softer US data cools Fed hike bets
item.description: The GBP/USD pair gains traction to near 1.3555 during the early European trading hours on Monday. The US Dollar (USD) weakens against the British Pound (GBP) as bets for a US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike come down.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah strengthens amid Prabowo's growth target, weaker US Dollar
item.description: USD/IDR extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 17,820 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair may face thin trading conditions as trading volumes remain subdued amid Indonesia’s Independence Day holiday.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Struggles near 159.00; seems vulnerable below 50% Fibo.
item.description: The USD/JPY pair attracts some sellers at the start of a new week, though it lacks bearish conviction and shows some resilience below the 159.00 mark during the Asian session.

item.title: Euro rallies to two-month high, eyes 1.1600 as USD struggles amid receding Fed hike bets
item.description: The EUR/USD pair builds on last week's bounce from the vicinity of the 1.1500 psychological mark and attracts follow-through buyers for the third straight day.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Edges higher above 113.00, bullish bias prevails above 100-day SMA
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross trades in positive territory near 113.00 during the early European session on Monday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) softens against the Australian Dollar (AUD) amid weaker-than-expected Japanese Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in India on Monday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Tests rising wedge bottom near 184.00
item.description: EUR/JPY depreciates after two days of gains, trading around 184.20 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: United States Dollar Index weakens to near 99.50 as traders push back Fed rate hike bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), an index of the value of the US Dollar (USD) measured against a basket of six world currencies, currently trades near 99.50 in the Asian trading hours on Monday. The DXY loses momentum as data showed US Retail Sales unexpectedly declined in July.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD bulls await acceptance above $66.00, 100-day EMA breakout
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) is seen building on Friday's bounce from mid-$63.00s and gaining some follow-through positive traction at the start of a new week.

item.title: Australian Dollar rises on hawkish RBA outlook
item.description: AUD/USD gains ground for the second successive day, trading around 0.7090 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair appreciates as the Australian Dollar (AUD) gains on the hawkish policy stance by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).

item.title: Canadian Dollar advances due to softer US Dollar, higher oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD extends its losses for the third consecutive day, trading around 1.3870 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair depreciates as the US Dollar (USD) declines amid weaker-than-expected US economic data and shifting central bank expectations.

item.title: WTI posts modest gains above $81.50 as traders weigh US-Iran deadlock
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $81.60 during the Asian trading hours on Monday. WTI remains volatile as talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have completely deadlocked.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar advances beyond 0.5900, highest since June 3 as USD stays weak
item.description: The NZD/USD pair attracts buyers for the second straight day and climbs above the 0.5900 mark, hitting a fresh high since June 3 during the Asian session on Monday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7873 vs. 6.7878 previous
item.description: On Monday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7873 compared to Friday's fix of 6.7878 and 6.7382 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains against weaker US Dollar following softer Q2 GDP data
item.description: USD/JPY loses ground for the second successive day, trading around 159.10 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair depreciates as the Japanese Yen JPY) remains stronger following the release of Japan’s preliminary Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data.
